verses.text: After this, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and took Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines.
He defeated Moab; and the Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.
David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah to Hamath, as he went to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates.
David took from him one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of them enough for one hundred chariots.
When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians.
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.
David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
From Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took very much brass, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the vessels of brass.
When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,

he sent Hadoram his son to king David, to Greet him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him (for Hadadezer had wars with Tou); and he had with him all kinds of vessels of gold and silver and brass.

King David also dedicated these to Yahweh, with the silver and the gold that he carried away from all the nations; from Edom, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
Moreover Abishai the son of Zeruiah struck eighteen thousand of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He put garrisons in Edom; and all the Edomites became servants to David. Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.
David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abimelech the son of Abiathar, were priests; Shavsha was scribe;
and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief officials serving the king.

footnotes.content: After a long season of waiting, David's victories come one upon another—Philistines subdued, Gath reclaimed. It strikes me how the Lord's promises don't rush, yet when they move, the momentum gathers. David's arm grew strong, but only because the Lord went before him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab brought under tribute—a shift from tribute paid TO David to tribute paid BY others. I've seen how a humble servant whom the Lord lifts up gains the ear of kings; not through pride, but through faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hadadezer and Zobah—a real power to be reckoned with. David pressed on as far as the Euphrates itself, establishing dominion through the will and strength of the Lord. Authority that rests on God's shoulder is the only kind that lasts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A thousand chariots taken, but David hamstrung the horses—keeping only a hundred. There's wisdom here: he chose to lean on the Lord, not on chariots. Even in victory, a faithful heart looks away from the weapons and back to the Giver.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twenty-two thousand Syrians fell when they marched to help Hadadezer. David didn't shrink at reinforcements; the Lord's hand was upon him regardless of the odds. Fear flees when you've tasted the faithfulness of God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Garrisons in Damascus, Syrians as servants—the refrain echoes: 'Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.' It's not David's prowess alone; it's the Lord's active hand. Grace accompanies the faithful step.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Golden shields brought to Jerusalem—treasures become sacred vessels when offered to the Lord. The spoils point beyond themselves, to the One who granted them. A wise heart turns victory into worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tibhath and Cun—real cities, real brass. The text reaches forward: this metal became Solomon's bronze sea and pillars, the very vessels of the Temple itself. Even the work of war becomes the foundation of God's house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tou king of Hamath heard the news and chose to align himself with the victor. Sometimes the wisest move is to recognize where the Lord's favor rests and turn toward it rather than against it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hadoram came bearing gold and silver, blessing the king. When a leader walks in righteousness, even distant rulers send gifts and honor. The Lord opens doors that no human hand could shut.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David dedicated the tribute to the Lord—from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistines, and Amalek. All these nations, once enemies or strangers, now sent gifts to the Lord's house. It reminds me that the Lord's reach is wider than any kingdom's grasp.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abishai struck eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Even a supporting hand shares the victory when the Lord is leading. I've learned that faithfulness often means standing beside the one called, not needing the spotlight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Garrisons in Edom, the Edomites serve David—and again the refrain: 'Yahweh gave victory to David wherever he went.' Readers today hear an echo in that promise: wherever you walk in humility and trust, His victory goes before you. Not conquest by strength, but by the faithfulness that the Lord honors.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David reigned over all Israel with justice and righteousness for all his people. Power that serves the weak bears the fingerprint of God. A king's strength is measured not by the size of his territory, but by how his people sleep at night.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joab over the army, Jehoshaphat as recorder—the offices of David's court. Each had his place, each served the kingdom. I've noticed that a wise leader surrounds himself with faithful servants, each gifted for their task.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zadok and Abimelech as priests, Shavsha as scribe—the spiritual and administrative life held together. A kingdom that honors both the altar and the word prospers. The sacred and the ordinary belong in one story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites, the sons of David serving as chief officials. Leadership runs through families, through trusted bonds. The Lord knit David's household into a network of faithfulness—each strand held by his hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
